{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Lipschitz convex finite-sum minimization with ball-restricted exact component values\par}\vspace{5pt}


\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{SO\_\allowbreak{}ZO\_\allowbreak{}E09c\_\allowbreak{}ball}



Single-objective optimization



Finite-population exact component-value queries are restricted to the feasible Euclidean ball. The expected-error frontier explicitly retains dimension, population size, and accuracy.



\textbf{Status.} Logarithmic gap



\textbf{TASK tags.} solution concept: Finite sum minimization; task family: Single objective



\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Convex; smoothness: Lipschitz



\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Exact; operation: Component function value; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared; scalar derivative order: Scalar function value (order 0)



\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed



\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} mode: Expectation; quantifier: Algorithm before instance



\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} budget: Fixed worst-case budget; measure: N component value



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}


Minimize \AtlasInlineMath{F(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x)} over the public Euclidean ball \AtlasInlineMath{X=B_2(0,R)} using selected component values.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}


Each fixed client function \AtlasInlineMath{f_i:X\to\mathbb R} is finite, convex, and \AtlasInlineMath{L}-Lipschitz in the Euclidean norm. Neither smoothness nor a shared minimizer is assumed. No definition or regularity outside \AtlasInlineMath{X} is required. Boundary minimizers are permitted.



The complete tuple \AtlasInlineMath{(f_1,\ldots,f_N)} is fixed before private randomization. Revisiting a client accesses the same function rather than a fresh stochastic loss.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}


One call selects \AtlasInlineMath{(i,x)\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\times X} and returns exactly one scalar \AtlasInlineMath{f_i(x)}. Both the client and the feasible point may be selected adaptively. Off-domain queries are not legal.



The public inputs are \AtlasInlineMath{d,N,L,R,\varepsilon}. A complete average, a group average, or a two-point difference must be computed from its actual component calls; no aggregate-value interface is supplied for free.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}


Return a measurable feasible \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat x\in X}, which need not have been queried.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}


The loss is \AtlasInlineMath{F(\widehat x)-F^\star}, where \AtlasInlineMath{F^\star=\min_{x\in X}F(x)}. Only this loss is averaged over the independent private seed.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}


Each selected scalar component value costs one call. The cap holds for every fixed seed and every possible scalar history, including initialization and verification. Internal computation, storage, projection, and operations on public domain geometry are uncharged. Communication rounds are not a resource of this comparison.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}


Queries, stopping decisions, and the output are measurable functions of the preceding transcript and an instance-independent private random seed. The unknown instance is fixed before the seed is realized. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.



Internal exact-real computation and storage using public inputs and received information are uncharged. The stated budget must hold on every execution path.




\AtlasMath{\forall(f_i):\ \mathbb E[F(\widehat x)-F^\star]\le\varepsilon}




The expectation is over the algorithmic seed after fixing all client functions. Every query and the output must be feasible, and the total component-value count is capped on every execution.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_worst\_case



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}


\AtlasInlineMath{d}: Ambient dimension \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{N}: Number of fixed client functions \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{N\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{L}: Uniform Lipschitz budget for every component \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{L>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{R}: Radius of the feasible and query ball \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{R>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}: Expected objective-error tolerance \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\rho}: Normalized inverse accuracy \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\rho>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\rho=LR/\varepsilon}



\AtlasInlineMath{\Lambda}: Logarithmic scale \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\Lambda>e}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\Lambda=e+d+N+\rho}



\AtlasInlineMath{d_\star}: Universal dimension threshold \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d_\star\in\mathbb N}.



Universal threshold in Theorem thm:main-rate.



\AtlasInlineMath{\rho_\star}: Universal inverse-accuracy threshold \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\rho_\star\in\mathbb N}.



Universal threshold in Theorem thm:main-rate.
